link.title: Starter: the bright-light analogue
link.summary: BB84's whole processing chain on light you can see: bits, bases, sifting, error rates, and an intercept station, on one desk.
bom: Site A and the intercept station
Photodiodes, BPW34 class, x2, with load resistors
3D-printed mounts, dark box or black card
stages: Run the twin with your measured readings.
Laser, two servo polarizers, photodiode, Arduino.
Aligned and crossed readings set the thresholds.
Add the station and watch the error rate climb toward 25 %.

link.title: The two-room single-photon link
link.summary: Weak 405 nm pulses at 0.5 photons, four polarization states, decoy pulses, four SiPMs, FPGA gating, free space across a hallway; a fiber classical channel carries the authenticated protocol. The twin predicts the clicks, errors, and key before you buy a part.
bom: Two fiber media converters and a 10–30 m duplex patch cord
Four 405 nm laser diodes (5 mW class) with a nanosecond pulse driver
Film polarizers, a half-wave retarder, neutral-density filters (OD 1–4)
Four non-polarizing beamsplitters and two polarizing beamsplitters
Four onsemi MicroFC-30035 SiPMs, breakouts, a 30 V boost module, four fast comparators
A coaxial cable or second fiber for the pulse clock
3D-printed mounts, black tubes, lens pairs, black card, felt
stages: Predict the bench and write a synthetic run ($0).
Laptops, media converters, fiber through the door (M1.1).
SiPMs, comparators, dark box; measure dark counts (M1.4).
Four diodes, polarizers, combiners, filters to μ = 0.5 (M1.5).
Passive basis choice, PBS arms, waveplate at 22.5°.
Clock over coax, gated counting, logs, twin check (M1.6).
Optional intercept-resend station in the hallway.

link.title: Entangled photons between the rooms (BBM92)
link.cost: $15,000–60,000 planning (itemized $10,500–53,000), or a borrowed teaching kit
link.summary: A down-conversion source shares polarization-entangled pairs between the rooms. A Bell test certifies the source; matched-basis outcomes make the key. Phase 2 borrows the source (risk MR-R3), and the same rig runs the photonic collapse code (M2.4).

stages: Waveplate, PBS, two detectors per room.

circuits.title: Can collapse carry a message? (P11)
circuits.summary: Alice encodes a bit in what she does to her half of entangled pairs; Bob, never told, tries to read it from his half. The exact density matrix shows why he cannot, and the leak control shows the analysis would notice a real channel.
bom: Open-plan processor time, about 10 minutes a month
stages: Aer with a noise model, and a fake device.
The free open plan; record calibration and layout.

parts.note: Builds the circuits; runs the simulator; submits jobs.

parts.label: Internet and the provider's queue
parts.note: Jobs travel as circuits; results come back as counts.

parts.label: Cloud processor (dilution refrigerator)
parts.note: A superconducting processor near 10 mK: free time on the open plan [ibm2026openplan].

parts.label: Qubit chip
parts.note: Pick neighbouring qubits for the circuit, and far ones for the crosstalk control.

circuits.claim: A measured upper bound on information per use; never a faster-than-light channel.

circuits.title: Teleportation and superdense coding (P12)
circuits.summary: Teleport the six cardinal states with two classical bits, then without them; send two bits on one qubit, then keep the qubit. Fidelity above 2/3 needs the bits.

circuits.title: Majorana parity teleportation (P13)
circuits.cost: $0 emulated; a partner lab for devices
circuits.summary: Measurement-only teleportation of Crogman, Dang, and Erenso (2025): two parity measurements and two classical bits give fidelity 1; one bit gives at most 2/3. The error budget maps device knobs to fidelity.
bom: Open-plan processor time, about 10 minutes a month

The free open plan; record calibration and layout.
